title: A Boy Who Loved to Learn
bigQuestion: How did a poor boy become a teacher people still read today?

story.title: Counting Grain by Lamplight
story.kicker: A poor boy works all day and still finds time to learn.
paragraphs: Long ago in China, a boy worked in a big barn. His job was to count the grain. He counted sacks of rice and millet. He wrote the numbers down with care.
His family was poor. His father had died when he was small. So the boy worked hard jobs. He did not complain. He did each job well.
At night, the boy did not just sleep. He practiced old songs. He learned old dances and old stories. He asked older people many questions.
The old stories say this boy grew up to be a great teacher. His name was Kong. Later, people called him Confucius. Many people remember him today.
story.think: The boy was tired after work. Why do you think he still wanted to learn at night?

lessons.title: Long Ago in Lu
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius lived in China about 2,500 years ago, in a small state called Lu.
reading: Confucius lived in China a very long time ago. It was about 2,500 years ago. That is longer ago than anyone can remember.
He lived in a small state called Lu. A state was like a small country. China had many states then. Each state had its own ruler.

words.d: a teacher who lived in China about 2,500 years ago

look.title: A Picture in Words
look.text: Look at a small town long ago. There are no cars. People walk on dirt roads. Oxen pull carts full of grain. Farmers work in green fields. A boy carries a basket to the barn.
look.prompt: What is different about this town and your town?

check.q: Where did Confucius live?
check.why: Confucius lived in China, in a state called Lu.

check.q: When did Confucius live?
check.why: Confucius lived about 2,500 years ago.

check.q: What was Lu?
check.why: Lu was a small state, like a small country, in old China.

lessons.title: His Name Means Master Kong
lessons.mainIdea: In China he is called Kongzi, which means Master Kong. In English we say Confucius.
reading: His family name was Kong. People in China call him Kongzi. That means Master Kong. A master is a wise teacher.
Long after he lived, people in Europe spelled his name in Latin. They wrote Confucius. English speakers still use that name today.

words.d: the Chinese name for Confucius; it means Master Kong
a wise teacher people look up to

look.title: One Teacher, Two Names
look.cite: Common spellings of the teacher's name
look.prompt: Which name has the most letters?

check.q: What does Kongzi mean?
check.why: Kongzi means Master Kong.

check.q: What is a master in this story?
check.why: Here a master means a wise teacher.

check.q: Which name do English speakers use?
check.why: In English we call him Confucius.

lessons.title: A Poor Family
lessons.mainIdea: The old stories say Confucius grew up poor, and his father died when he was small.
reading: The old stories say his father died when Kong was very young. His mother raised him. They did not have much money.
Being poor was hard. But Kong kept going. He helped his family. He learned from everything around him.

look.title: A Picture in Words
look.text: Look at a small house with one room. A mother cooks rice over a fire. A boy sits on a mat. He is holding a bamboo strip with words on it. He is trying to read it.
look.prompt: What does the boy want to do, even with little money?

check.q: Who raised Kong after his father died?
check.why: The old stories say his mother raised him.

check.q: Was Kong's family rich or poor?
check.why: The stories say his family was poor.

check.q: What did Kong do when life was hard?
check.why: He kept going, helped his family and kept learning.

lessons.title: Many Small Jobs
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius said he learned to do many simple jobs because he was poor when young.
reading: As a young man, Kong did many jobs. The book Mencius says he kept records of grain. It says he also cared for farm animals.
Later, Confucius talked about this. He said he was poor when young. So he learned to do many simple things well.

words.d: work a person does, often to earn money

look.title: Confucius Remembers
look.text: When I was young, my family was poor. So I learned how to do many plain, simple jobs.
look.cite: Analects, book 9, passage 6, retold simply from James Legge's translation (1861)
look.prompt: Why did Confucius learn many jobs?

check.q: What job does the book Mencius say Kong had?
check.why: The book Mencius says he kept records of grain.

check.q: Why did Kong learn many simple jobs?
check.why: In the Analects he says he was poor when young.

check.q: What else did Kong care for?
check.why: The book Mencius says he also cared for farm animals.

lessons.title: At Fifteen
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius said that at fifteen he set his heart on learning.
reading: Confucius once told his life story in a few lines. He said that at fifteen, he set his heart on learning.
To set your heart on something means you really want it. You keep trying. Confucius kept learning his whole life.

words.d: finding out new things and getting better at them

look.title: His Life in a Few Lines
look.text: At fifteen, I set my heart on learning. Then, year by year, I grew wiser.
look.cite: Analects, book 2, passage 4, retold simply from James Legge's translation (1861)
look.prompt: How old was Confucius when he set his heart on learning?

check.q: What did Confucius set his heart on at fifteen?
check.why: In Analects 2.4 he says he set his heart on learning at fifteen.

check.q: What does 'set your heart on' mean?
check.why: It means you really want something and keep trying.

check.q: How long did Confucius keep learning?
check.why: Confucius kept learning his whole life.

lessons.title: Anyone Can Love to Learn
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius taught that loving to learn is something anyone can do.
reading: Confucius did not say he was born knowing things. He said he loved old wisdom and worked hard to learn it.
He also said that in any small town, someone is as honest as he is. But not many love to learn as much. Loving to learn is a choice anyone can make.

words.d: knowing what is good and wise to do

look.title: Not Born Knowing
look.text: I was not born knowing things. I love the old wisdom, and I work hard to find it.
look.cite: Analects, book 7, passage 19, retold simply from James Legge's translation (1861)
look.prompt: What did Confucius say about how he got his wisdom?

check.q: Did Confucius say he was born knowing things?
choices: No, he worked hard to learn
check.why: In Analects 7.19 he says he was not born knowing and worked to learn.

check.q: Who can love to learn, as Confucius taught?
check.why: Confucius taught that loving to learn is something anyone can do.

check.q: What did Confucius love?
check.why: He said he loved the old wisdom.

lessons.title: Students Wrote It Down
lessons.mainIdea: After Confucius died, his students wrote down his words in a book called the Analects.
reading: Confucius had many students. They listened closely to him. After he died, they remembered what he said.
His students, and their students, wrote his words down. The book is called the Analects. Many lines start with 'The Master said.'

words.d: the book of Confucius's sayings, written down by his students
a person who is learning from a teacher

look.title: A Picture in Words
look.text: Look at a group of students sitting in a circle. One says, 'I remember what the Master said about friends.' Another writes it on a strip of bamboo. The strips pile up.
look.prompt: Why would students want to write down their teacher's words?

check.q: Who wrote down Confucius's words?
check.why: His students and their students wrote them down.

check.q: What is the book called?
check.why: The book of his sayings is called the Analects.

check.q: How do many lines in the Analects start?
check.why: Many lines start with 'The Master said,' meaning Confucius.

lessons.title: Still Read Today
lessons.mainIdea: People in China and around the world still read the Analects today.
reading: The Analects is very old. But people still read it. Children in China learned it by heart for hundreds of years.
People in Korea, Japan and Vietnam read it too. Now it is read in English and many other languages. People talk about what it means.

words.d: knowing words so well you can say them without looking
